summary: This note is a biographical sketch of Raghunath Dhondo Karve, covering his family background, birth in Murud, and education at New English School, Pune and Fergusson College. It describes his early career as a mathematics professor at Wilson College in Mumbai. It also explains that he was asked to resign after publicly advocating family planning, population control, and women's sexual rights, after which he devoted himself to those causes.
one_line: Biographical note on Raghunath Dhondo Karve, a Chitpavan Brahmin educator who lost his Wilson College professorship over his advocacy of family planning and women's sexual rights.
key_facts: Raghunath Dhondo Karve was born into a Chitpavan Brahmin family.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve was the eldest son of Bharat Ratna Maharshi Dhondo Keshav Karve.
His mother Radhabai died during childbirth in 1891, when Raghunath Dhondo Karve was nine.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve was born in Murud.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve studied at New English School, Pune.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve stood first in a matriculation examination conducted in 1899.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree from Fergusson College, Pune in 1904.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve started his professional career as a professor of mathematics at Wilson College in Mumbai.
Raghunath Dhondo Karve publicly expressed views on family planning, population control, and women's right to experience sexual/sensual pleasure as much as men.
The conservative Christian administrators of Wilson College asked Raghunath Dhondo Karve to resign from his professorship.
After leaving Wilson College, Raghunath Dhondo Karve devoted himself to family planning, population control, and women's sexual rights.
